title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
main_claim: Every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic. This would settle the Eskin–Fisher–Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture. The key input is Uniform Bounded Height: for a connected, simply connected, real-triangulable, unimodular Lie group G, every (K,C) self-quasi-isometry F satisfies ||πF(g) − πF(1) − A_F π(g)|| ≤ B(G,K,C), where A_F lies in a finite group 𝒜_G ≤ GL(W).
coverage:
I read all the main sections: models, boxes, polynomial, stationary, profiles, labels, offsets, uniformity, boundary and recognition. I did not read the Lipschitz appendix in detail. Steps checked line by line:

(1) Recognition deduction. Unimodularity from metric Følner sets. The homomorphism property of h ↦ A_h. The amenable-mean correction to a homomorphism τ with bounded defect. Polynomial growth of finitely generated subgroups of ker τ via bounded-height path packing, then Gromov. The FP_∞ / type F / Poincaré duality (PD) transfer chain (Li, Kropholler–Martínez-Pérez–Nucinkis, Bieri 9.23) is used with plausible hypotheses.

(2) Box calculus and packing. The basis-exchange bounds, path-packing upper bound, fixed-sheet lower bound and lift multiplicity are correct. The support-symmetry group is finite because it consists of isometries of the polyhedral norm p.

(3) Stationary slopes. The slope l is the projection of the cocycle onto constants. Cornulier–Tessera vanishing of reduced cohomology gives a sublinear L² estimate. The volume comparison gives P(πE) ≤ P(lE), hence l = Aπ. I verified the inverse coupling algebra: M = m×μ is domain-invariant by unimodularity, and the identity Ψ(U_yη) − Ψ(η) = −πy + Aπq_y(η) + R holds, giving exactly A^{-1}.

(4) Profiles. Occupation invariance through the interior-slack gap c·s₋ > m·s₊. The convex-increment constraint. The segment volume inequality via the backward-recurrence lemma (I checked its Cauchy–Schwarz and mass recursion). The affinity criterion: derivative labels lie in 𝒜 by strict convexity and the finite-union-of-subspaces argument; the support–variation equality fixes weight signs; extremal rays of chambers give line-affinity; Hörmander then gives smoothness.

(5) Neighbor labels. Facet agreement forces A₁⁻¹A₂ to be a reflection. I checked that P(E'₁ ∪ E'₂) = 2P(E). The target-side polynomial image argument is valid because union-scaled letters lie in the limiting embeddings.

(6) Neighbor offsets. The cone-quotient Haar multipliers ℓ_S, the tile count e^{r(P₁−P₂)}, the per-tile bound e^{r(P₂ − ℓ(b₂−b₁))}, the reverse inequality by swapping, and the conclusion that two-generator traces span W*.

(7) Uniformity. The point-mass argument, scale telescoping and basepoint comparison.

(8) Bounded height. Boundary maps from the uniform sublinear estimate with summable contraction. The image-volume sandwich F(x)·V₋ ⊂ f(x·U) ⊂ F(x)·V₊. Bounded variation along N-fibers via ray ideals plus the positive ray relation. Haar averaging on the nilpotent quotient.

Not independently re-derived: the exact exponents in the polynomial-image lemma, every diagonalization in the neighbor-labels contradiction (extending profile convergence to the facet by equicontinuity as δ_m → 0), and the precise statements of the cited theorems (Cornulier–Tessera Cor. 1.9, Kropholler–Martínez-Pérez–Nucinkis Thm 1.1, Li Cor. 4.47/4.48), which I could not check against the sources. These seemed sound as written, and I found no step that fails.
